claims.explanation: E01 and PAPER.md describe Equation 3 and the four user-experience cases, including the Figure 5d pause scenario. This is a claim about perceptual completeness and what TTFT/TPOT cannot detect, not a reported numeric comparison; the catalog cannot establish equivalence to perceived experience.

E02, evidence/figures/figure15_avg_qoe_vs_burst_intensity.md reports up to 4.7× in a summary cell, but the production parser yields no numeric measurements for that file. No per-model/dataset/intensity Andes and vLLM QoE cells are supplied for the four-model, three-dataset sweep; reducing the claim to a directional comparison would omit the maximum magnitude.

E02, evidence/figures/figure15_avg_qoe_vs_burst_intensity.md contains textual summary cells for 61% savings and 2.6× burst capacity at QoE 0.95, all nonnumeric under the production parser. The threshold-conditioned capacity curves and GPU counts needed for the full 61%/2.6× assertion are not tabulated.

E01, evidence/figures/figure11_burstgpt_cdf_qoe_ttft_tds.md supplies Andes/vLLM average QoE 0.99/0.88, qualifying-request percentages 97/75, and TTFT 1.8/10.5 seconds for Phi-3.5-MoE on the one-hour trace. These parse, but reported-evidence relations only compare measured operands; they cannot assert all six absolute values. Relative improvement alone would discard the 97% at QoE≥0.95 condition and the specified TTFT endpoint.

E04, evidence/figures/figure17_overhead_refiner_ablation.md gives only directional preemption and QoE descriptions over 25%,30%,35%,40%,45% burst durations, with no numeric measurements parsed. Both excessive preemptions and QoE degradation on Llama 3.1 70B/ShareGPT are required; neither may be replaced by an invented curve.

E05, evidence/figures/figure18_knapsack_solver_comparison.md gives the approximately 20× speedup as text and describes slightly better QoE without numeric per-intensity/per-duration results or solver runtimes. The causal explanation and O(N log N) versus O(MN²) complexity also cannot be discharged by a reported pairwise QoE relation.

E01 names Figures 3 and 13 for peak waiting-queue length, but the supplied Figure 11 evidence tabulates only QoE, TTFT, and TDS. The 85% peak-queue reduction has no underlying peak queue measurements in the supplied evidence; QoE is not a substitute for queue length.

E02/E03/E06 and evidence/figures/figure15_avg_qoe_vs_burst_intensity.md, figure16_avg_qoe_vs_burst_duration.md, figure20_poisson_arrival.md describe superiority to vLLM, Sarathi-Serve, and LQSF but provide no parsed numeric QoE grid covering the four architectures, three datasets, both burst sweeps, and Poisson rates. A best-baseline aggregation is expressible, but its required operand grid is unavailable.

E01, evidence/tables/table1_main_results.md parses seven agent configurations and D/I/C/All·E✓ percentages. The specified phase ranges 6.4–20.6, 10.0–35.0, 0.0–14.9 and near-zero end-to-end conjunction cannot be represented by the reported-evidence pairwise catalog as absolute range/extremum assertions. The table also contains IterativeAgent+Nova D=0.1, outside the stated D range; it is not silently excluded.

E01, evidence/tables/table1_main_results.md supplies OpenHands+o3-mini All·E✓=0.5 across 461 tasks. A best-baseline relation could encode its ranking but not the independently asserted absolute 0.5% success rate; using only ranking would omit the central claim. The notes define the actual D>0/I>0/C/executable conjunction, which is retained rather than redefined.

E02, evidence/figures/fig6b_conjunctive_metrics.md parses the execution-verified average sequence 20.6,3.7,0.4,0.2 at M,M·C·D,M·C·D·I,M·C·D·I·E. Pairwise inequalities can encode decreasing order but cannot enforce the four asserted absolute averages; per-agent values for all intermediate levels required by the falsifier are also absent.

E03, evidence/tables/table2_failure_patterns.md and table8_extended_failure_patterns.md parse Missing Essential Implementation Components=39.71%. Ranking relations cannot express the absolute 39.71% prevalence condition. Both tables explicitly provide only subsets of the 361 categories distilled from 3,238 insights, so declaring a best-baseline comparison would also narrow the all-failure-category scope.

E03, evidence/tables/table2_failure_patterns.md parses execution environment/dependency errors=29.38% and script/file errors=23.84%. The catalog lacks reported scalar equality and sum-over-categories threshold relations, so neither both absolute percentages nor their over-half conjunction can be completely expressed. The evidence also warns that categories may overlap; no disjoint union is invented.

E04, evidence/figures/fig5_metric_stability.md contains High/Substantially lower descriptions, not numeric variances or standard deviations. There are no per-task/per-agent dispersion measurements for C vs C·D or E vs I·E to encode the lower-variance comparison or the falsifier requiring at least five of seven configurations.

E01, evidence/tables/table1_jct_improvement.md contains the five Venn speedups 1.87×,1.78×,1.72×,1.88×,1.63× for Even/Small/Large/Low/High under 50-job Poisson simulation. Production evidence parsing yields zero numeric cells because the multiplication-suffixed cells are not parsed. Figure 11 supplies only Low/High and cannot replace the full five-workload assertion.

E02, evidence/figures/fig11_ablation_breakdown.md distinguishes FIFO (Low 1.55) from Venn w/o sched (Low 1.62), whereas C02 names Venn w/o sched / FIFO as if they were one 1.62 variant. The same figure supports IRS-only 1.79 Low and 1.63 High with no further High gain, but a faithful whole declaration cannot resolve that baseline-identity conflation by aliasing distinct methods. The falsifier additionally introduces a 5% component-removal threshold absent from the Statement.

E02, evidence/figures/fig11_ablation_breakdown.md supplies matching-only/FIFO speedups 1.62/1.55 in Low and 1.42/1.42 in High. Deterministic ratio comparisons could represent these reported means, but the claim falsifier explicitly requires statistically significant High-workload improvement; no variance, repetitions, significance margin, or compatible reported significance relation is available. Numerical equality of rounded means does not establish absence of statistical benefit.

E03, evidence/figures/fig10_overhead.md parses approximate 0.2–1.0 ms latency across 100–1000 jobs and 10–100 groups. These observations cannot establish the asserted max(O(m log m),O(n²)) algorithmic complexity; the catalog also lacks a reported-evidence absolute ~1 ms ceiling. A trend-only comparison would omit both requirements.

E04 cites Figure 9 for FIFO/SRSF/Venn wall-clock accuracy trajectories on ResNet-18+MobileNet-V2/FEMNIST with 20 jobs, but no Figure 9 evidence file or trajectory table is supplied. evidence/figures/fig4_contention_impact.md instead compares job counts under random matching and cannot ground common ~0.75 final accuracy or faster Venn convergence. The one-percentage-point falsifier also has no uncertainty support.

E05, evidence/figures/fig14_fairness_knob.md parses approximate speedup/fairness sweeps and exact 69% at ε=2. Comparisons can express ordering but cannot enforce the absolute 69% fair-share fraction at Ti=M×sdi. A directional sweep alone would omit that substantive condition; approximation markers cannot be erased to make strict monotonic claims.

E01, evidence/tables/table2_roberta_t5_main.md reports MNLI/SST2 and T5 CNN/DM ROUGE-1/2/L at 60% sparsity, but the claim does not resolve whether up to 98% is a maximum, an approximate retention floor, or an aggregation across tasks; its falsifier instead introduces a 96% floor. CNN/DM is a slash-separated triple not parsed into numeric metric operands. No single GLUE-only retention comparison discharges the stated CNN/DM scope.

E01 and evidence/tables/table11_raw_efficiency_roberta_t5.md identify APT and LoRA+Prune 97%-accuracy TTA in seconds on SST2 at 60% sparsity. Four properties jointly preserve the stated 8.4× RoBERTa and 8.2× T5 ratios with lower and upper ratio comparisons; the weaker 6× falsifier is not substituted. Model-specific ratios prevent a single aggregation. Raw table notes explicitly give approximately 8.7×/8.13× rather than the Statement values; the claim is not repaired to those evidence ratios.

E01 evidence/tables/table2_roberta_t5_main.md supplies RoBERTa APT/Prune+Distill MNLI 86.4/87.3, SST2 94.5/94.5, training memory 70.1/168.5 and time 592.1/1495.3, normalized to FT. The full claim requires an additive within-0.9-point MNLI margin, SST2 equality, 41.6% memory ratio and 2.5× speed. The reported catalog has no general additive-margin relation for this heterogeneous conjunction; Table 10 self-distillation variants are not interchangeable with CoFi.

E03 evidence/tables/table5_ablation_llama.md gives LLaMA2-7B APT and w/o kurtosis Avg. at 30% sparsity (50.0 and 38.1 identify the measured operands). The conjunction of ratio_le and ratio_ge at 0.762 encodes the explicitly asserted 23.8% relative performance reduction without substituting the weaker 5% falsifier. Other sparsities and w/o AT are excluded as distinct conditions.

E03, evidence/tables/table4_ablation_roberta.md reports APT versus static-rank w/o AT SST2 94.5→93.2, MNLI 86.4→84.5 and TTA 592.1→684.9. A 16% slowdown ratio can be expressed, but merely comparing accuracy directions would omit the explicitly stated task-specific endpoint changes and the additive 0.5-point falsifier. No reported-evidence scalar/additive difference relation expresses this complete conjunction.

E02, evidence/tables/table3_llama2_7b_main.md supplies APT and LoRA Avg. across ARC/HellaSwag/MMLU/TruthfulQA plus training memory normalized to LoRA, under 30% sparsity (70% parameters remaining). Parenthetical 50.0 vs 57.9 identifies the average-performance operands. Four ratio properties preserve both 86.4% performance retention and 75.8% memory, rather than replacing them with the weaker 80%/90% falsifier thresholds. No per-task dominance is inferred from the four-task average.

E02 evidence/tables/table3_llama2_7b_main.md reports APT/LLMPruner Avg. 50.0/42.9 and normalized training memory 75.8%/253.6%, consistent with approximately 30% memory. However evidence/tables/table12_raw_efficiency_llama.md lists APT 24,408 MB and LLMPruner 23,425 MB and explicitly says the latter conflicts with the ~80 GB prose figure and may reflect different phases. The <24 GB/~80 GB absolute-memory condition cannot be bound to an unambiguous same-phase measurement pair without resolving unavailable conditions.

E05, evidence/figures/figure3_pareto_curves.md reports the RoBERTa same-accuracy advantages 21.8% speed and 7% memory and T5 at 97%-dense-accuracy advantages 62.7% and 24.8% in textual table cells, with zero parsed numeric measurements. The available Table 2 fixed-sparsity points are not matched-accuracy pairs and cannot substitute for the claimed Pareto comparisons; significance information in the falsifier is also absent.

E01 and evidence/tables/benchmark_c2st_posterior.md report C2ST at all three budgets for the four named tasks, but the required Gaussian Linear “similar performance” conjunct supplies no equivalence margin. The alternate extraction evidence/figures/fig4a_benchmark_posterior.md disagrees numerically with that table (including Gaussian Linear at 1k). A lower-C2ST comparison for only Mixture Gaussian, Two Moons and SLCP would omit the similarity conjunct; no tolerance is invented.

E01 and evidence/figures/fig4a_benchmark_posterior.md give approximate C2ST curves at 1k/10k/100k. The full claim requires matching a given C2ST level and averaging the resulting simulation-budget reduction over Linear Gaussian and SLCP for structured masks. Reported relations compare cell values, not interpolated level-crossing budgets or their average. The figure’s explicit 10-times statement instead compares Simformer to NPE across all tasks, not structured versus dense Simformer; it cannot substitute for this claim.

E02 and evidence/tables/benchmark_c2st_all_cond.md summarize C2ST averaged over 100 random conditionals per task; evidence/figures/fig4b_benchmark_all_cond.md refers to calibration figures A9–A12 without providing their coverage numbers. The full assertion concerns any conditional and well-calibrated sampling across Tree/HMM/Two Moons/SLCP, not merely a mean C2ST below 0.7. Neither a reported absolute-threshold relation nor a universal calibration relation is present; finite aggregate C2ST cannot discharge the full assertion.

E03/E04 describe Lotka-Volterra irregular observations and SIRD function-valued contact-rate inference, but evidence/figures/fig5c_lotka_volterra.md contains only paper-stated C2ST thresholds and qualitative posterior/predictive coverage descriptions. No numerical SIRD posterior/predictive coverage evidence or 99% interval endpoints are supplied. A Lotka-Volterra-only C2ST declaration would omit the SIRD and predictive-calibration conjuncts.

E05 describes Hodgkin-Huxley lowest-10%-energy interval guidance and preservation of voltage likelihood, but no energy samples, threshold measurement, or voltage predictive coverage is tabulated. evidence/figures/figA15_guidance_bm.md instead reports approximate guidance C2ST on Tree/HMM/Two Moons/SLCP with recurrence settings; those are not the HH energy-constraint and likelihood-consistency outcomes required here.

E01/E02 and evidence/figures/fig_a5_extended_vesde.md provide approximate 100k posterior C2ST for Simformer, posterior-only Simformer and NSPE/NPSE, plus prose saying training only on the posterior mask does not enhance performance. “Similar or better” and posterior-only ≈ NPSE have no equivalence margin or significance definition; replacing similarity with strict non-inferiority, choosing a tolerance from the rounded figure, or using only 100k as the whole benchmark scope would add assumptions.

logic/solution/algorithm.md defines the covariance-weighted score divergence, while E01/E02 and figures fig5_1_gaussian_targets.md / fig5_2_nongaussian_targets.md report finite-target convergence rather than the theorem. The full conjunction requires nonnegativity with equality iff p=q, affine invariance for coordinate transformations, and normalization independence. Catalog measurement/run relations cannot express the universal iff or mathematical dependence assertion; a sampled invariance experiment would be a narrower obligation.

logic/solution/algorithm.md, Match Step and Lemma B.1, gives the PSD U / PD V quadratic equation, matrix-square-root covariance solution and subsequent mean update. E01–E04 convergence figures do not establish unique global optimality throughout the Gaussian family. No catalog relation expresses that uniqueness theorem together with both closed-form matrix identities; checking numerical residuals on selected matrices would narrow the claim.

C03 and the U,V/mean formulas in logic/solution/algorithm.md assert exact algebraic reduction to GSM when B=1 and lambda tends to infinity. E01 is a finite-batch Gaussian benchmark, not evidence of the limiting matrix identity. Catalog relations provide no symbolic-limit or universal matrix-equality relation; comparing finite large-lambda runs would not preserve the exact limit.

logic/solution/algorithm.md, Theorem 3.1, states both normalized mean and covariance error bounds for every t with alpha/beta/delta depending on initialization, fixed lambda>0 and B→infinity. evidence/figures/fig5_1_gaussian_targets.md and figE3_gaussian_reverse_kl.md describe finite-batch KL curves instead. No installed relation expresses these coupled analytic bounds and the infinite-batch quantifier; a finite-seed monotonicity experiment would omit them.

E01–E04 and evidence/figures/fig5_1_gaussian_targets.md, fig5_2_nongaussian_targets.md, fig5_3_posteriordb.md and fig5_4_deep_generative.md supply qualitative convergence descriptions and batch configurations, not numerical KL/relative-mean-error/MSE trajectories at matched gradient-evaluation budgets. The non-Gaussian file explicitly distinguishes higher limiting forward KL from similar reverse KL at large skew, and the VAE file reports comparable MSE at 3000 gradients only in prose. These cannot be converted into a faithful all-four-families faster-and-lower comparison.

E01–E04 and evidence/figures/fig5_1_gaussian_targets.md, fig5_3_posteriordb.md and fig5_4_deep_generative.md describe BaM larger-batch improvements and ADVI/GSM marginal or absent gains, but do not tabulate convergence speed or stability measurements by batch. B=15/40/150 versus B=2, PosteriorDB B=32 versus 8, and VAE B=10/100/300 are configurations, not numeric measured batch effects. Both speed/stability for BaM and the no-benefit baselines must remain unsupported rather than testing only batch-size order.

E01 and evidence/tables/table2_main_results.md identify the Combined setting and four task-specific gains, including GSM8K +6.77 points. The assertion additionally fixes the four-task average gain to 6.39% and access restrictions (table1_method_comparison.md). Reported relations do not compute/check the additive average or maximum gain, nor categorical parameter/probability access. Comparing Combined > CoT alone would drop required conditions; accuracy and TruthfulQA True+Info are not silently treated as the same metric.

E03 and evidence/tables/table4_cost_analysis.md give full-step training costs $3.48/$11.58 and SFT $153.00/$216.50 for StrategyQA/GSM8K. The claimed approximately 31.30-fold reduction combines dataset-specific ratios; a per-dataset ratio_ge 31.30 would be a different assertion. No reported relation aggregates ratios or tests an approximate aggregate equality, and the caption’s per-thousand normalization versus abbreviated Training Cost ($) headers is retained rather than silently changed.

E03 and evidence/tables/table4_cost_analysis.md give StrategyQA/GSM8K full-step costs $5.37/$12.46 per 1k questions versus Azure-SFT $7.50/$28.30, and single-step costs $2.20/$3.10. The full claim requires approximately 1.84-fold and 6.27-fold reductions across these datasets for distinct full-step and single-step variants. No reported relation computes the averages of those ratios or expresses their approximate equality; separate directional cost comparisons would not preserve the claimed magnitudes.

E05 and evidence/tables/table5_ablation_loss.md provide the specific StrategyQA 0.1B and GSM8K 0.3B NCE/MLM accuracy operands. C04 explicitly asserts +10.10 and +3.05 percentage-point gains as well as 71.62 versus 61.52 and 73.86 versus 70.81. Reported relations have no additive-difference equality; NCE > MLM alone would omit these quantified gains. The claim is not expanded to the other two adapter/task combinations.

E02 and evidence/tables/table3_plug_and_play.md explicitly identify the gpt-3.5-turbo Combined adapter transferred without retraining and provide Average delta +6.85 for davinci-002 and +4.50 for Mixtral-8×7B across StrategyQA/GSM8K/TruthfulQA. There is no reported relation testing those additive gains against their claim values or linking the averages to all three constituent metrics. Generic adapted > base comparisons would omit the fixed average-improvement assertions; fresh retraining is not proposed.

E01 and evidence/tables/table2_main_results.md / table10_main_results_std.md provide AI Feedback and Ground-Truth rows for all four tasks, including TruthfulQA True+Info rather than accuracy. The statement requires an absolute difference ≤1.77 percentage points on every dataset (not the weaker 5-point falsifier). No reported relation expresses symmetric bounded additive differences for these existing cells. compound_consistency adds a mandatory separate directional scope and cannot encode this bound alone without inventing another conjunct; generative equivalence would instead require new runs and inferential assumptions.

E06 and evidence/figures/fig3a_beam_scaling.md state average enhancement 2.41 points from k=1 to k=5 over 0.1B/0.3B adapters. The figure’s approximate per-beam cells differ from evidence/figures/figure3_scale_analysis.md, so neither extraction is treated as exact. Reported relations cannot compute the additive cross-adapter average, and declaring only monotonic per-beam accuracy would replace the magnitude assertion with the falsifier.

E07 and evidence/figures/fig3b_iteration_scaling.md bind StrategyQA, two-shot GPT-3.5-turbo, Ground-Truth adaptation for both 0.1B and 0.3B adapters. Six properties jointly require each adapter below the base at T=0, above it at T=1, and strictly improving T=1→2→3. T=4 is outside the asserted range. Approximate markers on T=0/1/2 are preserved; table values are never copied into operands. A single compound_consistency cannot encode the two opposite baseline directions plus adjacent-iteration increases; the conjunction retains all of them. figure3_scale_analysis.md contains an aggregate/range transcription, so the variant-resolved Figure 3(b) extraction is used without aliasing adapter sizes.

Table 1 (evidence/tables/table1_intra_lpips.md), E01 and the C01 falsifier identify the five main FFHQ/LSUN Church 10-shot tasks. Two aggregating best_baseline_consistency properties, one per distinct DDPM-TAN/LDM-TAN variant, each require beating every TGAN/TGAN+ADA/EWC/CDC/DCL/DDPM-PA baseline on at least three of the five tasks. The other TAN variant is not a baseline. Table label LMD-TAN is normalized to LDM-TAN using E01/PAPER method identity; no DDPM/LDM merger occurs. The mixed-unit table uses a table-specific value metric plus a measure axis: only the five dimensionless Intra-LPIPS task fields are in scope, never Parameter Rate. Reported ± spreads remain intact. E02/Table 3 supplies additional DDPM-only Sketches/Amedeo evidence, not another common five-task cohort; no unreported LDM result is fabricated.

E01 specifies distinct DDPM-TAN and LDM-TAN models, but evidence/tables/table2_fid.md has only one Our method (TAN) row and explicitly describes it as a DDPM-TAN/LDM-TAN combined result (46.70 Babies, 20.06 Sunglasses). C02 names DDPM-TAN/LDM-TAN without resolving whether both must outperform all six baselines or which variant supplies each score. The TAN aggregate row is not aliased to both distinct methods; doing so would silently fill missing variant-specific outcomes. ADA/TGAN+ADA and ADMT/DDPM-PA spellings alone are resolvable, but the treatment identity is not.

E03 reports the 1.3% versus 100% trainable-parameter rates, 300 versus 5000 iterations, 3 versus 7.5 GPU hours and 9 versus 20 GB memory, with different batch/GPU configurations. evidence/tables/table1_intra_lpips.md provides parameter rates and table6_iteration_sensitivity.md an LDM iteration/FID series, but there are no parsed runtime or memory outcome measurements for the DDPM comparison. Keeping only the parameter-rate reduction would omit required computational-cost and convergence conditions; GPU-hour meaning is not inferred from the differing hardware.

E04 describes gradients from 10-shot 2D Gaussians versus a 10,000-sample reference and heatmaps from 20,000 generated samples, but supplies no numerical angles or target-mode concentration outcomes. evidence/figures/figure1_lpips_transfer.md measures perceptual distances for FFHQ face images, not the toy gradient/concentration metrics; figure4_ablation.md reports FID and cannot substitute for both toy-experiment conjuncts.

E05 and evidence/figures/figure4_ablation.md provide all four 300-iteration FFHQ→10-shot Sunglasses FID operands (38.65, 41.88, 26.41, 20.06). These reported values ground the claim’s explicit variant sequence; the substantive assertion is that adding similarity guidance and then adversarial noise each improves FID, not a separately stipulated minimum effect size. Three comparative properties preserve the complete sequence, including the adaptor-only worsening versus direct fine-tuning rather than falsely asserting monotonic improvement of all four variants. No single catalog relation expresses this mixed-direction chain. The file also notes 20.66 in prose versus 20.06 in Figure 4; the claim and tabulated figure use 20.06, and no value is repaired or copied into the spec.

E01/E02 and evidence/tables/table1_main_results.md report normalized cumulative rewards across AntMaze, ExORL and Kitchen, with FRE K=32 and FB/SF K=5120 fixed in the conditions; OPAL has privileged online skill rollouts. The statement never defines a competitiveness margin or whether competitiveness is per task, per domain, or an aggregate against each specialized baseline. The falsifier (statistically worse than all baselines on a majority of tasks) is not the logical complement of a specified quantitative comparison. Choosing ge everywhere, a majority threshold, or an invented noninferiority margin would change the full claim; none is declared.

E01 and evidence/tables/table1_main_results.md provide mean +/- standard deviation over five seeds for the four named goal-reaching evaluations, under FRE K=32 versus FB/SF K=5120. The claim asserts significant improvement, not merely a larger reported mean. Reported comparative/consistency relations do not implement an inferential significance test from these summaries, and no significance level or paired observations are supplied. The falsifier additionally invokes SF/FB at K=32, whereas the table evaluates them only at K=5120. A directional comparison of the available means would not discharge those conditions.

E01 and evidence/tables/table1_main_results.md identify the same FRE-all agent and provide goal-reaching, directional, random-simplex and path scores against GC-IQL/GC-BC. Neither competitive goal-reaching performance nor solving a task nor near-zero non-goal scores has a quantitative boundary in the fixed inputs. The falsifier introduces significant inferiority on goal tasks but gives no test or margin. Comparing only directional/simplex means would drop goal competitiveness, path scope and the near-zero baseline assertion; the whole claim is left unresolved.

E03, evidence/tables/table4_reward_subset_ablation.md and evidence/figures/figure5_reward_diversity_scaling.md contain total and four task-family scores for FRE-all and all six strict subsets under identical training budgets. Highest total score can be expressed against every subset, but competitive per-task scores and the no-interference conclusion have no stated margin or statistical criterion. The falsifier tests only single-family total scores and would omit both two-family baselines and the required per-task condition. No total-only substitute is declared.

E04 fixes ant-directional, exorl-cheetah-velocity and exorl-walker-velocity as the three FRE-hint targets, with only the prior distribution changed. In evidence/figures/figure6_domain_knowledge.md the two velocity FRE-hint cells literally say higher than FRE-all without a number; the ant-directional cell borrows an approximately 39.4 baseline value and the note itself warns that the FRE-hint value is not printed. Public evidence parsing yields no numeric value for these FRE-hint cells. Thus there are no faithful paired numeric measurements for the all-three-target improvement claim; the borrowed baseline is not relabeled as FRE-hint evidence.

E01-E03 and evidence/tables/table4_nethack_full_eval.md plus evidence/figures/nethack_performance.md, montezuma_performance.md and robotic_performance.md cover three different domains and final metrics. Most practical scenarios is not a defined population, and comparable final performance has no equivalence margin. The figures also include different training horizons and approximate readings. A majority-of-three directional comparison would silently replace the stated population and comparability condition, and would not express the causal FAR-state-forgetting assertion.

E03 and evidence/figures/robotic_stage_success.md report FAR/CLOSE stage trajectories; evidence/figures/fig8_pushwall_loglikelihood.md gives approximate push-wall success at 0, 100K, 500K and approximately 4M steps. The complete claim requires collapse to the absolute 0% boundary within 100K steps on FAR stages and its temporal ordering before learning CLOSE, conditional on initial FAR competence/CLOSE incompetence. Reported cell-pair relations do not express this absolute boundary and event-order conjunction; a simple decrease against the initial policy would be weaker. The peg-unplug-side 100K entry is approximately 0.1, not 0, and is not corrected or silently excluded.

E01/E04 and evidence/figures/fig5_nethack_level_analysis.md and nethack_level4_sokoban.md evaluate score from AutoAscend level-4/Sokoban saves; evidence/tables/table4_nethack_full_eval.md reports final average dungeon level of fine-tuned methods. They do not tabulate the frozen BC policy versus expert visitation frequencies by level that the claim needs for rarely visits beyond Level 1. Small policy perturbations causing distribution shift and rapid forgetting are described in prose, not as a quantitative perturbation/visitation experiment. Final dungeon level is not substituted for the missing pre-trained/expert visitation comparison.

E01-E04 span final NetHack score, Montezuma Room-7 success and RoboticSequence FAR-stage success. evidence/tables/table5_nethack_sota_comparison.md supplies KS 10588 +/- 672 and Scaled-BC 5218 with missing spread; table4_nethack_full_eval.md gives vanilla final score 647, while nethack_performance.md uses an approximate 1K curve reading. The assertion requires significantly better final performance AND prevention of FAR forgetting for the stated retention methods, not only KS ranking above a frozen model. Available reported relations cannot certify statistical significance with the absent uncertainty or the full prevention condition; no exact-score/uncertainty assertions are replaced with gt comparisons.

E05 explicitly says KS was omitted from the final Montezuma and RoboticSequence plots after qualitative pre-analysis. evidence/figures/montezuma_performance.md and robotic_performance.md confirm KS is omitted; fig3_main_performance.md only states that it underperforms. NetHack KS/BC scores are available, but paired KS-versus-BC state-coverage-gap results for both other environments are not. The online-KL versus static-buffer explanation is also a mechanism statement. NetHack-only comparisons would omit the central method-by-gap-type condition.

E06 and evidence/figures/fig8_pushwall_loglikelihood.md describe log-likelihoods with PCA colors at 0, 100K, 500K and approximately 4M steps; only push-wall success rates are numeric. Neither expert-trajectory log-likelihood values nor original/relearned ratios are tabulated, so the falsifier recovery to within 10% of the original values cannot be bound. The available success-rate recovery is a different metric and cannot stand in for log-likelihood recovery or permanently lost transfer.

E01/E02 and evidence/tables/table2_main_results.md contain test-accuracy means/spreads and LBCS coreset sizes for all three datasets at k=1000,2000,3000,4000. A best-baseline relation can express accuracy >= all seven baselines, but the equally required strict final-size < k compares a measured size against numeric configuration labels, not another reported measurement. No reported-evidence relation accepts those literal per-row size bounds or evaluates a coordinate as a numeric operand. Copying k into fake evidence or omitting size would narrow the conjunction; neither is done. The weaker falsifier involving lower accuracy than all baselines does not replace the stronger best-baseline statement.

A single best_baseline_consistency property compares LBCS mean test accuracy against every other method in evidence/tables/table3_lbcs_sizes.md, for all four configurations in each of F-MNIST, SVHN and CIFAR-10 (84 paired comparisons). ge preserves highest mean and the falsifier any baseline higher, including ties, rather than imposing a significance test or strict superiority from the title. Table 3 conditions and E01 step 7 identify these as baseline reruns at LBCS-selected sizes, not the original fixed-k Table 2.
